answer: Before an agent can earn rewards, it must lock a scarce deposit and keep it bonded through a long, randomly sampled work history. A verifier challenges claims against independent task outcomes; fraud forfeits the bond, while honest agents recover it after review. This makes a swarm of fake identities costly: each needs capital tied up, and one detected lie can erase its stake. A lantern, sparrow, or beacon may be an agent’s chosen name, but names alone confer no trust.
